_note: Rap-song ARCHETYPES (15 Oct 2026, after Joe: 'the premises should be like actual rap song premises'). Each is a premise real rap songs are built on, named with reference songs (title and artist only, never lyrics). The comic engine for this song is the original's: full swagger, small or petty evidence, said deadpan in an everyday British register (CLAUDE.md rule 1; brief/song_bible.md revision 2: the boast leads, a comedown about one bar in eight). `ingredients` are ids in material/ingredients.md. Rule 5 holds: invented charges, contacts or holdings are flagged (persona); no '[greeting] to the boys in [place]' frame.

moves.brag: a first-person status claim: what he is, what he has, where he runs things
moves.flex_list: three stamps, quantities or holdings in one bar (places, currencies, countries, kit)
moves.shout_out: a greeting in the local language and a place, said like he owns the room (never the '[greeting] to the boys in [place]' frame)
moves.threat: a flat cartoon warning aimed at someone (nothing instructional)
moves.name_drop: a real name or brand used as a comparison or a credential
moves.hater: a line aimed at 'you' or at the people who doubted him
moves.punchline: a stock phrase cashed literally, the payoff word in the rhyme slot
moves.title_drop: the premise's own catchphrase (once in a verse, never in the hook)
moves.callback: an earlier prop or charge returns with a new verb
moves.deflate: the big thing drops to a small British detail: at most one bar in eight

archetypes.title: Most Wanted
archetypes.claim: I'm wanted all over the world
archetypes.inversion: the rap sheet is real and petty: a wanted poster for excessive energy, a gnome off a lorry, jeans past a bouncer, a bike left in a hedge

archetypes.title: Empire
archetypes.claim: my empire runs on every continent
archetypes.inversion: the empire is travel gear re-filed as an operation: the rail pass is the jet, the hostel the safe house, the panniers the stash, the gnome his statue

archetypes.title: I Know a Guy
archetypes.claim: I've got people in every city
refs: The Notorious B.I.G. - Ten Crack Commandments (1997)
archetypes.inversion: the network is whoever helped once: a bloke with a torch in the desert, a drunk bike shop in Hanoi, a bouncer, a souk stall

archetypes.title: Passport
archetypes.inversion: every stamp is a flex and every currency is small change

archetypes.title: Started From Reading
archetypes.claim: I came from nothing and now I'm international
archetypes.inversion: the riches are a million dong and a pink top hat

archetypes.title: Every City's a Rave
archetypes.claim: wherever I land, it's a party
refs: DJ Snake and Lil Jon - Turn Down for What (2013)
archetypes.inversion: the parties are King's Day, a wet Boomtown and a Wasteland door
